questions.stem: Rice in India is mainly a
questions.explanation: Rice needs high temperature and plenty of water. It is sown with the onset of the south-west monsoon and harvested in autumn, which makes it mainly a kharif crop. Rabi crops are sown in winter.

optionRationale.1: Rabi crops such as wheat are sown in winter.
optionRationale.3: Zaid crops are grown in the short summer season between rabi and kharif.
optionRationale.4: Plantation crops are tea, coffee and rubber.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a plantation crop?
questions.explanation: Plantation crops such as tea, coffee and rubber are grown on large estates with capital, labour and processing near the farm. Wheat, gram and barley are rabi food crops grown in ordinary farms.

optionRationale.1: Wheat is a rabi food grain.

questions.stem: The chief ore of aluminium is
questions.explanation: Aluminium is extracted from bauxite, a clay-like ore found mainly in laterite areas. Haematite is an iron ore, galena is an ore of lead and limestone is used in cement and in iron and steel.

optionRationale.2: Galena is an ore of lead.

questions.stem: Which type of coal has the highest carbon content and is of the best quality?
questions.explanation: Coal is ranked by its carbon content. Peat has the lowest carbon, then lignite, then bituminous. Anthracite has the highest carbon content, burns with little smoke and gives most heat. Hence the correct answer is: Anthracite.

optionRationale.4: Peat is the first stage with the least carbon.

questions.stem: In land use statistics, net sown area refers to
options: the total area sown, counting every sowing of the year separately and each crop on the field
the area sown with crops and orchards, counting an area sown more than once only once
the land left fallow and unsown during the year because of poor rainfall or soil
the area under forests and permanent pastures
questions.explanation: Net sown area counts every piece of land once, however many crops are taken from it in a year. Gross cropped area counts the land again for each crop. Cropping intensity is the ratio of gross cropped area to net sown area.

optionRationale.4: Forest area is a separate land use category.

questions.stem: Tank irrigation is most important in
options: the canal-fed plains of Punjab and Haryana, where canals and tubewells dominate
the dry sandy tracts of the Thar desert and the arid parts of western Rajasthan
the peninsular plateau states such as Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh
questions.explanation: In the peninsula the undulating rocky surface and impervious soils favour the building of tanks to store rain water. In the northern plains canals and wells are more important. Hence the correct answer is: the peninsular plateau states such as Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

optionRationale.1: Canals and tube wells dominate in Punjab.
optionRationale.2: The Thar has little water to store in tanks.
optionRationale.4: High mountains rely on streams, not tanks.

questions.stem: Cultivable land left uncultivated for more than one year but less than five years is called
options: net sown area of the year
questions.explanation: Land left uncultivated for one agricultural year is current fallow. If it is left for more than a year and less than five, it is fallow other than current fallow. Beyond five years it becomes culturable waste.

optionRationale.1: Current fallow is land left for one year or less.
optionRationale.2: Net sown area is the area actually sown.
optionRationale.3: Culturable waste land has been left uncultivated for more than five years.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a target area programme in India's planning?
options: Green Revolution in the wheat and rice growing regions
Operation Flood for the growth of milk production across the country
Public Distribution System through fair price shops
questions.explanation: Target area planning deals with regions that have special problems. Hill Area, Drought Prone Area and Command Area Development programmes belong to it. The others are national schemes aimed at crops, milk and food supply.

optionRationale.2: The Green Revolution is a national agricultural strategy.
optionRationale.3: Operation Flood is a dairy programme.
optionRationale.4: The Public Distribution System is a national food scheme.

questions.stem: The widely used definition of sustainable development was popularised by the report
questions.explanation: The Brundtland Commission's report Our Common Future (1987) defined sustainable development as development that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. Hence the correct answer is: Our Common Future.

optionRationale.1: Silent Spring dealt with pesticide effects.
optionRationale.3: Limits to Growth dealt with resource and population limits.
optionRationale.4: The Human Development Report ranks countries by human development.

questions.objective: Recall the origin of sustainable development

questions.stem: A district has a net sown area of 40,000 hectares and a cropping intensity of 125 per cent. How much area is sown more than once?
questions.explanation: Cropping intensity is gross cropped area divided by net sown area, times 100. So gross cropped area is 125 per cent of 40,000, or 50,000 hectares. The area sown more than once is 50,000 minus 40,000, which is 10,000 hectares.

optionRationale.1: 5,000 hectares would need a cropping intensity of about 112 per cent.
optionRationale.2: 50,000 hectares is the gross cropped area, not the repeated area.
optionRationale.4: 20,000 hectares would need a cropping intensity of 150 per cent.

questions.stem: In a district the reporting area is 60,000 hectares and the area under forests is 18,000 hectares. What percentage of the reporting area is forest?
questions.explanation: The share of forests is the forest area divided by the reporting area, times 100. That is 18,000 divided by 60,000, times 100, which is 30 per cent. Hence the correct answer is: 30 per cent.

optionRationale.1: 25 per cent is a wrong division.
optionRationale.2: 33.3 per cent would need 20,000 hectares of forest.
optionRationale.3: 18 is the number of thousand hectares, not the percentage.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Excessive irrigation in arid and semi-arid areas can make soils saline and waterlogged.
Reason (R): Water evaporates at the surface and leaves salts in the upper soil layers, and drainage is often poor.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: When too much water is applied without proper drainage, the water table rises and evaporation leaves salts behind in the topsoil. This process makes soil saline and waterlogged, so R explains A.

optionRationale.2: R is the direct explanation of A.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Planning in India began with the First Five Year Plan in 1951.
Reason (R): The NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Both statements are factually correct. However, the 2015 change in the planning body has no bearing on why planning began in 1951, so the reason does not explain the assertion.

optionRationale.1: R does not explain why planning began in 1951.
optionRationale.3: A is true, so option 3 is wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so option 4 is wrong.

questions.objective: Recall facts about planning in India

questions.stem: Match List-I (crop) with List-II (leading producing state).
questions.explanation: Assam leads in tea (I), Karnataka in coffee (II), West Bengal in jute (III) and Kerala in rubber (IV). These crops are linked to the climate and soils of those states.

right: I. Better use of irrigation water in canal areas
II. Reducing the effect of recurring drought
III. Using local resources in hilly areas
IV. Development of a tribal region in Himachal Pradesh

questions.explanation: The Command Area Development Programme aims at better use of irrigation water (I), the Drought Prone Area Programme deals with recurring drought (II), the Hill Area Development Programme uses local hill resources (III) and Bharmaur is a tribal area in Himachal Pradesh (IV).

optionRationale.1: It swaps drought and hill programmes.
optionRationale.2: It swaps command area and drought programmes.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about water resources in India.
A. Irrigation is the largest user of water.
B. Per capita availability of water falls as population rises.
C. Rainwater harvesting can help recharge groundwater.
D. Water scarcity is caused only by low rainfall.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Irrigation takes the largest share of water, per capita availability falls as population grows, and harvesting rain recharges groundwater. D is wrong, because over-use, pollution and rising demand also cause scarcity.

optionRationale.1: Option 1 leaves out A, which is correct.
optionRationale.2: Option 2 leaves out B, which is correct.
optionRationale.4: Option 4 includes D, which is wrong.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about minerals.
A. Iron ore and manganese are ferrous minerals.
B. Bauxite is the ore of aluminium.
C. Mica is a metallic mineral.
D. Copper is a non-ferrous metal.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Iron ore and manganese are ferrous minerals, bauxite is the ore of aluminium, and copper is a non-ferrous metal, so A, B and D are correct. Mica is a non-metallic mineral used mainly in electrical goods, so statement C is wrong and option 3 is the right choice.

optionRationale.1: Option 1 leaves out D, which is correct.
optionRationale.2: Option 2 includes C, which is wrong, and leaves out D.
optionRationale.4: Option 4 includes C, which is wrong, and leaves out A.

questions.stem: Fragmentation of landholdings is a problem in Indian agriculture because it
options: makes mechanisation and efficient irrigation difficult on tiny plots
raises the average size of the holdings
reduces the number of farm households
increases the net sown area of the whole nation
questions.explanation: When holdings are divided among heirs, plots become small and scattered. Machines cannot be used well and irrigation, supervision and travel between plots become costly, which lowers efficiency. Hence the correct answer is: makes mechanisation and efficient irrigation difficult on tiny plots.

optionRationale.2: Fragmentation reduces the average size of holdings.
optionRationale.4: It does not by itself increase the net sown area.

questions.objective: Explain a problem of Indian agriculture
